title: Composition
description: JSON Schema for a composition — the partial binary operation ∘ : Hom(B, C) × Hom(A, B) → Hom(A, C) that pairs two transformers and produces their composite (Mac Lane 1971 Ch. I §1). A composition instance is the triple (first-morphism, second-morphism, composite). The domain-codomain matching condition — codomain of first equals domain of second — is a categorical property checked by a separate transformer, not expressible in JSON Schema (cross-field reference). Composition is associative and admits identity morphisms as neutral elements; these laws are also transformer-level checks.

first-morphism.description: The first morphism f: A → B in the composition g ∘ f.

second-morphism.description: The second morphism g: B → C in the composition g ∘ f. Its domain must equal the codomain of first-morphism for the composition to be defined.

composite.description: The composite morphism g ∘ f: A → C. Its domain equals the domain of first-morphism; its codomain equals the codomain of second-morphism.
